question.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
question.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 5x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =5x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 5\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

judgment.reasoning: All 16 selected answers agree with the captured MA conclusions and are mathematically correct. Two worked solutions contain authored errors: q-41957 uses -3 instead of +3 in the quadratic-formula numerator for x^2-3x+3=0; its discriminant is nevertheless -3, so there is no real intersection and p+q is undefined. In q-20804, an extra minus sign before the limit incorrectly negates F(0)-F(a); the correct half-integrals are -\pi/6 and +\pi/6, giving zero. For the other questions: q-86791 completes to (y+2)^2-(x-2)^2/16=1; q-49610 gives (125-27)/6=49/3; q-107795 expands (x-1)(x-2)(x^2-16); q-17317 factors as (x+1)(x-4)(x^2+4), leaving roots ±2i; q-3471 sums the intersection coordinates to 2/5; q-124166 requires discriminant 16+8k=0, hence k=-2, with valid tangency at x=1; q-115836 is positive exactly between -5/2 and 2 because x^2+3 is always positive; q-14449 and q-114312 follow by integration by parts and differentiate back to their integrands; q-115227 has no solutions because its left side exceeds 4; q-118776 has convergent half-integrals -1/6 and +1/6; q-81707 satisfies both v'(t)=-6e^{-2t} and v(0)=2; q-15133 and q-103831 use polar speed sqrt(r^2+(dr/dtheta)^2), with derivatives 12cos(4theta) and -12sin(3theta), respectively. No prior submission or grade is supplied; each MA answer is supported by its own captured worked solution.
